summary: Citation coverage is dense overall (all 27 bib entries cited), but three paragraph-specific gaps remain: the upper-bound/auditing positioning of the verified sizes, the corruption-robust ranking comparator family for flip perturbations, and benchmark context for the NBA sports design.
missing_literatures: exact, greedy, and certified algorithms for worst-case data dropping and accuracy limits of one-step influence approximations
rank aggregation from pairwise comparisons under adversarial corruption or poisoning
paired-comparison and Bradley-Terry ratings of sports teams

rewrite_targets.reason: The paper's main interpretive caveat is that every reported size is an upper bound from a one-step influence ordering, and that the true minimum 'may be smaller, possibly by a lot'. The 'What a verified size means' paragraph supports this with a single citation (low-dimensional OLS auditing). The 'Upper bounds, not minima' limitation paragraph has no citation. Reviewers who know the drop-data literature will expect the follow-up work on algorithms that tighten or certify drop-data sets and on documented failure modes of the one-step approximation. That work bears directly on how loose the reported sizes might be.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Computing $k^\star$ is a combinatorial search problem. Provable auditing is known only in special settings ... (also Discussion: 'Upper bounds, not minima')
search_topics: failure modes of approximate maximum influence perturbation for worst-case data dropping
greedy or exact algorithms for finding minimal data-dropping sets that overturn a conclusion
robustness auditing lower bounds certificates for small data subsets in regression

rewrite_targets.reason: The flip perturbation is explicitly motivated as modeling 'mislabeled or adversarially cast votes'. The manipulation paragraph cites only one paper on attacks against rank aggregation (HodgeRank/spectral) plus LLM-specific vote rigging. The neighboring literature on ranking from pairwise comparisons when a fraction of the comparisons is adversarially corrupted is the natural theoretical comparator for the flip results, and it is not cited.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Adversarial attacks on rank aggregation have also been analyzed as games between attacker and aggregator
search_topics: rank aggregation from pairwise comparisons with adversarial corruptions
data poisoning attacks on Bradley-Terry or BTL ranking from pairwise comparisons

rewrite_targets.reason: NBA seasons are one of the four evaluation designs and drive the headline count-scale finding (7 and 16 games; one game moves the top-5 set). The only sports citation is Elo's 1978 book on chess ratings. Nothing cites paired-comparison or BT modeling of team sports, so the sports design reads as an unmotivated add-on next to the well-cited LLM designs.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: NBA games from two seasons of the FiveThirtyEight Elo record ... each game a comparison between two teams
